entries.title: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets, with two offering exemptions and a conditional investment-contract safe harbor
entries.facts: On August 18, 2026 the SEC announced it proposed new rules, titled Regulation Crypto Assets, that would create a framework for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets. The proposal includes a one-time exemption from Securities Act registration permitting offerings of up to $5 million during a four-year period, and a second exemption permitting offerings of up to $75 million during each 12-month period. Under both exemptions issuers would be required to make certain principles-based narrative disclosures available to investors, and issuers under the second exemption would also be required to provide financial statements and be subject to ongoing reporting requirements. The proposal further includes a conditional safe harbor from the term investment contract in the definitions of security in the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and would preempt state securities law registration and qualification requirements for securities issued under a Regulation Crypto Assets exemption as well as certain secondary market transactions. The public comment period will remain open for 60 days following publication of the proposing release in the Federal Register.
entries.relevant_to: token issuers, crypto exchanges, digital asset fundraising platforms, securities counsel

entries.title: CFTC announces supplemental consent orders against former Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison and Alameda and FTX co-founder Gary Wang
entries.facts: On August 19, 2026 the CFTC announced the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered supplemental consent orders against Caroline Ellison, former Alameda CEO, and Gary Wang, former Alameda and FTX co-founder. The orders require Ellison and Wang to continue cooperating with the Commission, impose a five-year trading ban and a 10-year registration ban on Ellison, and impose a five-year trading ban and an eight-year registration ban on Wang, with the bans running from the date of entry of the initial consent orders entered December 23, 2022. The supplemental orders acknowledge the Commission is not seeking restitution, disgorgement, and/or civil monetary penalties at this time, a decision based in part on the level of Ellison's and Wang's cooperation in the Commission's investigation and related proceedings, including the parallel criminal actions in which each pled guilty to several criminal charges, and the $11.020 billion forfeiture order in those criminal actions for which they were jointly and severally liable. The initial and supplemental consent orders resolve the CFTC's enforcement actions against Ellison and Wang.
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital asset trading firms, enforcement and white-collar counsel

entries.title: CFTC proposes part 4 amendments adding CPO and CTA registration exemptions and raising the small pool threshold
entries.facts: On August 18, 2026 the CFTC published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeking public comments on amendments to part 4 of the CFTC's regulations, addressing registration requirements for commodity pool operators and commodity trading advisors, with the stated aim of reducing duplicative and overlapping regulation. The proposed rule would add an exemption from CPO registration for certain investment advisers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in relation to commodity pools for which the participants are limited to certain sophisticated investors and which meet other conditions discussed in the proposal, add a related registration exemption for commodity trading advisors, and increase the capital contribution threshold in the current CPO registration exemption for small commodity pools, known as the small pool exemption, to reflect inflation. Comments will be accepted for 45 days following publication in the Federal Register.
entries.relevant_to: commodity pool operators, trading advisors, digital asset fund managers, registered investment advisers

entries.issuing_body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
entries.title: Comptroller Gould says a GENIUS Act final rule will be out by November and that 23 of 40 new charter applications involve digital asset activity
entries.facts: On August 19, 2026 the OCC announced that Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould discussed the agency's work to support the Administration's efforts to grow the economy and lead the global digital currency revolution, in a Fireside Chat at the Wyoming Blockchain Symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. In the excerpts released by the OCC, Gould stated that the agency has received 40 new bank charter applications since President Trump took office, that over half of them, 23 of 40, involve some form of digital asset activity, and that on the GENIUS Act, quote, We will have a final rule out by November.
entries.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, de novo bank charter applicants, crypto custody providers, bank regulatory counsel
